stem: An 11-year-old boy has three weeks of right thigh pain and warmth with low-grade fever. X-ray shows a lytic lesion in the mid-shaft of the femur with layered periosteal reaction. A biopsy is taken.
oneliner: 11M + thigh pain + low-grade fever + mid-shaft lytic femur lesion + layered periosteal reaction → which histologic pattern?

options.A: Sheets of small uniform round blue cells with scant cytoplasm and no matrix
options.B: Spindle cells directly producing pink bone matrix
options.C: Cells with vacuolated scalloped nuclei and fat droplets
options.D: Pale cells with grooved nuclei mixed with eosinophils
options.E: Sheets of cells with eccentric nuclei and clock-face chromatin

whyNot.B: **Osteoid production** defines osteosarcoma, usually at the metaphysis with a sunburst pattern
whyNot.C: **Lipoblasts** mean liposarcoma, a soft-tissue tumor of adults
whyNot.D: **Langerhans cells with eosinophils** (CD1a) make a punched-out lesion, usually skull or flat bone, without layered periosteum and fever
whyNot.E: **Plasma cells** mean myeloma, a disease of older adults, not an 11-year-old

why: **Ewing sarcoma** arises in the **diaphysis** of children and shows **sheets of small, uniform round cells** with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio and **no matrix**. **Onion-skin periosteum** and fever mimic osteomyelitis; it carries **t(11;22) EWS-FLI1**.

idea.rule: Diaphyseal bone tumor in a child with small round blue cells and no matrix is Ewing sarcoma.
also: Cells are PAS positive from glycogen and CD99 positive
Neuroblastoma, lymphoma and rhabdomyosarcoma are other small round blue cell tumors
Responds to chemotherapy; arises from neuroectodermal-type cells
